title: metrics
description: One run's result (metrics.json), as scripts/_record.py builds it. dataset_id and build are REQUIRED: a number without the data it measured and the build that produced it cannot be compared to anything. Every field the harness writes is declared here, and nothing else is accepted: a field from another version would otherwise pass silently while nothing reads it.

purpose.description: What the pass was for (RFC-032 step 4): the run, a repeat of it, a pair-test side, or a re-timing on another machine. Absent: a run.

started_at.description: When the pass started: written before its first item, so a stopped run still says when (run.json).

prompt_versions.description: The prompt versions the run sent, by name (RFC-032 step 4b): what the adapter's prompts(params) gave, of the prompt_sha256 its fingerprint declares.

machine.description: The operating system a pass ran on, from its fingerprint's runner (named by a re-timing's label).

of.description: The run a repeat, pair or retime is of, when exactly one other run of the system on the dataset exists.

actor.description: Who acted (RFC-027): a person, or an agent and the person it acted for. A recorded claim, not an identity.

for.description: the person an agent acted for

created_at.description: When this record's scores were computed: the measurement, or for a derived run the derivation.

build.description: The SYSTEM UNDER TEST. Without this a delta cannot be attributed to a code change.

dirty.description: Was the system-under-test tree dirty? null = UNKNOWN, which is the honest value when the ref is self-declared (EVAL_BUILD_REF) rather than read from a checkout. It was hardcoded false there, asserting a clean tree on no evidence; null and false are different claims and the schema must admit both.

scores.description: Aggregate metrics. Keys are yours; values must be numbers.

params.description: The knobs the arm actually ran with.

adapter.description: Which adapter scored these numbers: a path from the project (or the repository root in a checkout), `scripts/adapter.py` for the bundled one, `imported:<scorer>` for import-run.

metric_kinds.description: The adapter's reading of its metrics.

metric_directions.description: Metrics that improve going down or up, as the adapter (METRIC_DIRECTIONS) or import-run --asc declared.

metric_descriptions.description: What each metric measures, as the adapter (METRIC_DESCRIPTIONS) declared: one line, or a summary and details for the metric's own catalog page.

primary_metric.description: The metric that answers 'which arm is better'.

reference_tier.description: What the run was scored against: a reference's tier, or labels (a label set, RFC-023).

reference_coverage.description: Recorded when only some items have a reference: quality metrics are means over items_with_reference, not items.

fingerprint.description: What the number depended on, and one hash over it (scripts/_fingerprint.py).

warmup_ms.description: The adapter's warm-up, kept out of the per-item latency.

providers_seen.description: Which upstream providers answered, and how often.

resume.description: What a resumed run replayed from the pass it resumed.

history_confound.description: A replay's items where the variant met a human reaction recorded after an action production took and it did not (RFC-031 P1): its score there partly reads a reaction to another decision. The ids are in confound.jsonl beside it, never for a held-out side.

not_scorable.description: Items left unscored because their label holds only under production's action and this run acted otherwise (RFC-031 L3): no observed outcome of its own.

failed_items.description: Items whose call failed (not transiently): scored as an empty answer or the adapter's score_failure, the pass went on (A5).

imported.description: import-run: the source file and its coverage of the dataset.

rescore_dropped_metrics.description: rescore: metrics the source recorded and the current scorer no longer emits.

source_created_at.description: A derived run: when the run it was derived from was measured.

derived.description: A run computed from another run's stored outputs: what did it, from which run, when, with what.

from_dir.description: The source run's directory under the data directory (RFC-024): a derived run reads its outputs from there, and from no other run of the same name.

with.description: What computed it: the adapter and scorer hashes (rescore), the judge scorer (judge), the parser (reparse).

source.description: The source's own derived block, when it was itself derived.

goal.description: The goal this run answers, from its config: data/goals/<goal_id>.yaml (validate V14).

round.description: The round of its goal this run belongs to, from its config (ADR-0004, optional).

model_record.description: The model record its config named (RFC-020, optional): data/models/<id>.yaml, whose settings it ran with.

deployment_id.description: The deployment of that record its config named (RFC-021, optional): an id in the record's `deployments`.

format.description: The output format the config asked for; must be one the goal's output_contract accepts (validate V14).

expect_identical_to.description: The config this run must reproduce item for item, from its config (a regression guard): validate V5 checks it does.

run_metrics.description: The metrics in scores that the adapter's score_run() computed over the whole run (one number each, no per-item values): shown by the leaderboard and compare, never tested item by item.

hypothesis.description: The hypothesis block of the run's config (ADR-0025): what the arm was expected to do against which config on which measure. Outside the fingerprint.

hypothesis_in_advance.description: Whether that hypothesis was committed before the run: named is true, false, or null (not determinable: not in git, a build that is not a commit, a dirty tree); commit and committed_at are the commit that last changed it.

faithfulness.description: A replay's faithfulness when it ran (RFC-030): the latest record of its code record on its dataset, whether it lets the replay be scored, and who scored it anyway with --unfaithful.

record.description: <code_id>/<n>, or null when none was made

repeat_index.description: Which repetition this is, when measuring an arm's own variance.
